source: RFC 0005 §5.1, RFC 0006 §5.3.1 (round 2 review of host and tools, M2)
statement: An http action no request can have does not compile, in a statement, a rate limit rule or the short-form action of a catalog entry (as RoleExpansion.effective writes it out): http:HEAD, since a HEAD request is decided as GET (PIP-18), and an http verb holding an ASCII lower-case letter, since a method that holds one is refused before any decision. The message names the action and says to write http:GET, or the verb in upper case. http:*, upper-case verbs and the verbs of other services stay valid. The data plane and the control plane compile with the one compiler, so a stored document with such an action is installed as failed, and the control plane refuses a change that makes one; the schema says the same.
guards: engine:PolicyCompilerTest#an http action no request can have does not compile
